# Source evidence for #5448 -- "Organize usage of GetResourceFromHandle and
# GetResourceFromVal calls in validation"

Ground truth: main-debug, source tree confirmed identical to public upstream
89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df outside this skill directory
(version-verification.txt). All line numbers below are from
lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp and lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidationUtils.h
at that commit.

## 1. Both names still exist, unrenamed, exactly as the issue describes

lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidationUtils.h:109
  DxilResourceProperties GetResourceFromVal(Value *resVal);

lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp:167-189
  static DxilResourceProperties GetResourceFromHandle(Value *Handle,
                                                      ValidationContext &ValCtx) {
    CallInst *HandleCall = dyn_cast<CallInst>(Handle);
    if (!HandleCall) {
      if (Instruction *I = dyn_cast<Instruction>(Handle))
        ValCtx.EmitInstrError(I, ValidationRule::InstrHandleNotFromCreateHandle);
      else
        ValCtx.EmitError(ValidationRule::InstrHandleNotFromCreateHandle);
      DxilResourceProperties RP;
      return RP;
    }

    DxilResourceProperties RP = ValCtx.GetResourceFromVal(Handle);
    if (RP.getResourceClass() == DXIL::ResourceClass::Invalid)
      ValCtx.EmitInstrError(cast<CallInst>(Handle),
                            ValidationRule::InstrHandleNotFromCreateHandle);
    if (RP.Basic.IsReorderCoherent &&
        !ValCtx.DxilMod.GetShaderModel()->IsSM69Plus())
      ValCtx.EmitInstrError(HandleCall,
                            ValidationRule::InstrReorderCoherentRequiresSM69);

    return RP;
  }

So `GetResourceFromHandle` is exactly what the issue says it should stop being:
a function that both looks up resource properties AND emits validation errors
as a side effect, under a name that gives no hint it can mutate diagnostic
state. `GetResourceFromVal` (DxilValidation.cpp:266-274) is the silent lookup
the issue says should be the only thing individual op validators call.
No function named ValidateResourceHandle exists anywhere in the tree
(confirmed: `git log --all -i --grep=ValidateResourceHandle` and a tree-wide
grep both return nothing -- see below).

## 2. The up-front validation pass the issue asks for already exists...

lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp:559-583
  // Make sure none of the handle arguments are undef / zero-initializer,
  // Also, do not accept any resource handles with invalid dxil resource
  // properties
  void ValidateHandleArgsForInstruction(CallInst *CI, DXIL::OpCode Opcode,
                                        ValidationContext &ValCtx) {
    for (Value *op : CI->operands()) {
      ...
        if (isa<UndefValue>(op) || isa<ConstantAggregateZero>(op)) {
          ValCtx.EmitInstrError(CI, ValidationRule::InstrNoReadingUninitialized);
        } else if (ArgTy == pHandleTy) {
          // GetResourceFromHandle will emit an error on an invalid handle
          GetResourceFromHandle(op, ValCtx);
        }
    }
  }

Called from ValidateHandleArgs(...) (line 585), which is called unconditionally
for every resource dxil op at DxilValidation.cpp:2283, inside the same
dispatch function that later calls ValidateResourceDxilOp(...) at line 2321
for the resource-touching opcodes (GetDimensions, Sample*, BufferLoad/Store,
TextureLoad/Store, CBufferLoad*, RawBuffer*). There is no early return between
the two calls -- both run against the same CallInst.

## 3. ...but the per-op accessors still call the error-emitting function again

lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp:191-236 (GetSamplerKind,
GetResourceKindAndCompTy) and :547-557 (GetCBufSize) -- the exact three
functions the issue names -- all still call GetResourceFromHandle, not
GetResourceFromVal:

  static DXIL::SamplerKind GetSamplerKind(Value *SamplerHandle,
                                          ValidationContext &ValCtx) {
    DxilResourceProperties RP = GetResourceFromHandle(SamplerHandle, ValCtx);
    ...

  static DXIL::ResourceKind
  GetResourceKindAndCompTy(Value *Handle, DXIL::ComponentType &CompTy,
                           DXIL::ResourceClass &ResClass,
                           ValidationContext &ValCtx) {
    ...
    DxilResourceProperties RP = GetResourceFromHandle(Handle, ValCtx);
    ...

  static int GetCBufSize(Value *CbHandle, ValidationContext &ValCtx) {
    DxilResourceProperties RP = GetResourceFromHandle(CbHandle, ValCtx);
    if (RP.getResourceClass() != DXIL::ResourceClass::CBuffer) {
      ValCtx.EmitInstrError(cast<CallInst>(CbHandle),
                            ValidationRule::InstrCBufferClassForCBufferHandle);
      return -1;
    }
    return RP.CBufferSizeInBytes;
  }

For an invalid handle reaching e.g. GetDimensions: ValidateHandleArgs (step 2
above) already ran GetResourceFromHandle on that same Value and emitted
InstrHandleNotFromCreateHandle once; ValidateResourceDxilOp's GetDimensions
case then calls GetResourceKindAndCompTy -> GetResourceFromHandle on the
identical Value again and emits InstrHandleNotFromCreateHandle a second time.
This is precisely the "any errors emitted there will now be emitted twice"
architecture the issue describes -- it is still the current architecture, not
a historical one.

## 4. Some call sites already use the pattern the issue asks for -- the
##    inconsistency itself is confirmed, not just the double-emission

lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp:1572-1579 (ValidateASHandle, used for
TraceRay's acceleration-structure handle) already does exactly what the issue
requests: call the silent GetResourceFromVal, check validity itself, and emit
its own single, specific diagnostic instead of relying on GetResourceFromHandle's
generic one:

  static void ValidateASHandle(CallInst *CI, Value *Hdl,
                               ValidationContext &ValCtx) {
    DxilResourceProperties RP = ValCtx.GetResourceFromVal(Hdl);
    if (RP.getResourceClass() == DXIL::ResourceClass::Invalid ||
        RP.getResourceKind() != DXIL::ResourceKind::RTAccelerationStructure) {
      ValCtx.EmitInstrError(CI, ValidationRule::InstrResourceKindForTraceRay);
    }
  }

Lines 2383 and 2655 (ValCtx.GetResourceFromVal(Handle) / GetResourceFromVal(Handle))
are two more call sites already using the silent accessor directly. So the
codebase today contains both styles side by side -- exactly the "mess" the
issue's title names -- rather than having settled on one before or after
filing.

## 5. DxilResourceProperties::isValid() exists and is never called from the
##    validator (include/dxc/DXIL/DxilResourceProperties.h:79,
##    lib/DXIL/DxilResourceProperties.cpp:34-36):

  bool DxilResourceProperties::isValid() const {
    return getResourceKind() != DXIL::ResourceKind::Invalid;
  }

grep for `.isValid()`/`->isValid()` in lib/DxilValidation/DxilValidation.cpp:
zero matches. Every call site instead repeats
`RP.getResourceClass() == DXIL::ResourceClass::Invalid` (or the resource-kind
equivalent) by hand -- consistent with the issue's ask that callers "should be
using GetResourceFromVal() and IsValid()", which they are not.

## 6. No commit has ever implemented any part of this refactor

  git log --all --oneline -i --grep="GetResourceFromHandle"    -> 0 commits
  git log --all --oneline -i --grep="ValidateResourceHandle"   -> 0 commits
  git log --all --oneline -i --grep="5448"                     -> 0 commits
  git log --all --oneline -S"ValidateResourceHandle" -- lib/DxilValidation
                                                                -> 0 commits

## 7. Filing context: this is a same-day follow-up to a merged PR, not an
##    independent bug report

  gh pr view 5399 --repo microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler --json mergedAt,state
    -> {"mergedAt":"2023-07-22T01:06:04Z","state":"MERGED"}
  issue.json createdAt: "2023-07-22T01:12:41Z" (6 minutes after PR #5399 merged)
  issue body: "Full context can be seen here:
    https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/pull/5399#discussion_r1269919402"

PR #5399 ("Prevent instructions that accept handle arguments from accepting
malformed handle arguments") is exactly ValidateHandleArgsForInstruction /
ValidateHandleArgs above -- the up-front pass this issue's reporter had just
added, and immediately flagged as leaving the rest of the file's
GetResourceFromHandle/GetResourceFromVal split unreorganized.

## 8. No cross-references, no comments (fetch: comments=0; timeline: labeled/
##    added_to_project_v2/milestoned events only, no cross-referenced events)

## 9. Why this cannot be tested with a dxc.exe command line

The duplicate-diagnostic consequence described in section 3 requires a
resource handle Value that is a CallInst but is absent from ValCtx.ResPropMap
(i.e. not a recognised CreateHandle/CreateHandleFromBinding/AnnotateHandle
result) reaching a resource dxil op. Ordinary HLSL cannot construct that
Value: the only source-level way to make a handle come from something other
than a single static CreateHandle call is to select dynamically between two
different resource objects, and DXC's own legalizer rejects that before DXIL
validation ever runs -- confirmed directly:
control-dynamic-handle-select.hlsl selects between two Texture2D locals and
main-debug rejects it with `local resource not guaranteed to map to unique
global resource` at exit 0x80004005, an ordinary diagnosed error
(captured via `triage.py run --issue 5448 --args "-T cs_6_0 -E main
control-dynamic-handle-select.hlsl" --label control` ->
variant-control-main-debug.txt), before the validator's
GetResourceFromHandle path is ever reached.

Reaching the validator's own bad-handle path (an operand that IS a CallInst
of the handle type but was never entered into ResPropMap) needs directly
hand-authored malformed DXIL, tested through the standalone validator (`dxv`)
rather than dxc.exe's full compile-then-validate pipeline. `dxv.exe` is not
built in this environment (build\Debug\bin has only clang-tblgen, dxc,
FileCheck, llvm-tblgen), and building it is a new build target -- out of
scope, since this task explicitly disallows rebuilding anything. match.json
and cmd.txt are therefore deliberately not created for this issue (per
SKILL.md: "match.json and cmd.txt may be deliberately absent when compiler
output cannot answer the question; do not manufacture a hollow predicate
merely to make the directory look complete"), and godbolt is skipped for the
same reason -- Compiler Explorer only compiles well-formed source through the
same front end that already blocks this path, so a link would show nothing
beyond what the control above already shows.
